Add a Dutch dashboard, screenshots and install steps

The Dutch dashboard has a live view with trend graphs on the vitals tiles,
sock status and active Owlet alerts, and a trends view with the last 12
hours, sleep, daily statistics and battery. Its entity ids follow the Dutch
entity names, the test translates them through nl.json and checks them
against the created entities.

The README shows screenshots of it at the top and explains step by step how
to find the entity id prefix and install either dashboard.

Ship the Owlet API client inside the integration

Vendor pyowletapi-ng (lucasvollebergh/pyowletapi, commit 8e50ede) into
custom_components/owlet/owletapi so Home Assistant no longer installs an
external pyowletapi from PyPI. The client keeps refreshed tokens, makes
fewer requests per poll, retries once on rejected tokens and maps network
errors and timeouts to OwletConnectionError.

- manifest: no requirements, no external logger
- replace the compat layer with OWLET_CREDENTIAL_ERRORS in const
- run the client's own tests as part of the integration test suite
- ruff per-file ignores keep the vendored code identical to the fork
- README, CHANGELOG and NOTICE updated

Write APP_ACTIVE again as soon as the base station reports it went idle

Measured on a Dream Sock: the base uploads vitals for about 45 seconds
after APP_ACTIVE is written, then sets the flag back to 0 itself and
stops, so a fixed 60 s cadence left a gap every minute. The client now
re-activates whenever the cloud shows APP_ACTIVE at 0, and the activation
interval (default now 30 s) is only a ceiling. Release 2026.10.1.

Treat rate limits and server errors as transient, back off, and persist tokens regardless

429 and 5xx from the Owlet cloud and the login services (including the
"too many attempts" lock-out) raise OwletRateLimitError or
OwletConnectionError and delay the next poll (honouring Retry-After, then
exponential backoff with jitter up to five minutes) instead of starting a
reauthentication. Token refreshes are serialised with a lock, refreshed
tokens are stored even when the poll failed, unreadable responses are
connection errors, and device discovery no longer writes APP_ACTIVE.

Decode properties by type, survive bad fields and map the Dream Sock's status properties

Values are decoded explicitly (null alerts are unknown, not off; sentinel
readings such as a heart rate of 0 or a 255 ten minute average are None),
unreadable vitals, sock version or timestamps no longer break the update,
version detection retries, and DISCOMFORT_ALRT, LOW_INTEG_READ, the four
PREVIEW_*_PRIORITY_ALARM flags, BASE_MON_STATUS, BATTERY_STATUS and the
RED_ALERT_SUMMARY timestamp are exposed as entities.

Write APP_ACTIVE on a configurable cadence, after the read, never blocking it

New Activation interval option (default 60 s, 10 to 600) passed to the
client, so APP_ACTIVE is written once per interval instead of before every
poll. The property read happens first and no longer depends on the write:
a transient failure of the write is logged and retried on the next poll.

Allowlist diagnostics, react only to real alert transitions, document the fork

Diagnostics include only known-harmless fields (region, options, normalised
values, and raw values for vitals, alerts, status and firmware properties),
so nothing Owlet adds later can leak identifiers. The alert blueprint fires
only on off to on, the dashboards' "no alerts" card requires every alert to
be off, blueprint source URLs point at this repository, and the README
explains what this fork does differently and why.

Fix duplicate integration entries for same email across different regions (#1)

The unique_id for config entries was based solely on the email address,
which prevented users from creating entries for the same account in
different API regions (europe/world). Changed the unique_id format to
include the region prefix (e.g. "europe_user@example.com") and added a
v1->v2 migration that updates existing entries automatically.

Bump pyowletapi to 2025.4.10 and fix Home Assistant compatibility

pyowletapi 2025.4.2+ removed OwletPasswordError and OwletEmailError. Both
were already dead code: Firebase collapsed INVALID_PASSWORD, INVALID_EMAIL
and EMAIL_NOT_FOUND into a single INVALID_LOGIN_CREDENTIALS, so only
OwletCredentialsError can still be raised.

* Pin pyowletapi==2025.4.10. Everything the integration uses (get_devices,
  Sock.update_properties, control_base_station, the property maps and the
  region endpoints) is unchanged between 2025.4.1 and 2025.4.10.
* Catch OwletCredentialsError during setup. It was not caught at all, so a
  credentials error escaped instead of triggering the reauth flow.
* Catch OwletCredentialsError during reauth. A wrong password used to fall
  into the generic handler and the form came back without an error message.
* Drop the now unreachable invalid_email and invalid_password strings and
  add the missing no_devices string, which the config flow already sets but
  no translation file defined.
* OptionsFlow.config_entry is a read-only property in current Home
  Assistant, so assigning it raised AttributeError and broke the options
  dialog. Removed the __init__ override.
* Reload the config entry when options change, otherwise a new polling
  interval only took effect after a Home Assistant restart.
* Coordinator read CONF_EMAIL from the config entry, but the config flow
  stores CONF_USERNAME, so an expired token raised KeyError instead of
  starting reauth.
* Add a release workflow that builds the HACS owlet.zip on tag push and
  verifies the tag matches the manifest version.
